arguments.name: Naturalistic theories fail to explain the minimal facts
arguments.conclusion: Naturalistic theories cannot adequately explain the minimal facts, and most critics have given up on them.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: The minimal facts can refute every naturalistic theory (S647, S644).
P2: Most critics today have given up naturalistic theories (S649, S691).
P3: Bart Ehrman says history can neither prove nor disprove miracles (S698-S701).
P4: More critical scholars now accept either a bodily resurrection or a real (Casper) appearance experience rather than denying the resurrection (S731).

st1.quote: Most critics today have given up naturalistic theories.

st2.quote: If you take this approved list, you can refute you can give the major reputations of every naturalistic theory.

st3.quote: Why did James Crossly say, "I'll grant all six and I'm just not in the faith."

st4.quote: These six facts, throw the empty tomb in there, seven or take the 12, the longer list of which the empty tombs part.

st5.quote: But somebody else might have done it. It could be a critical comeback.

st6.quote: Most critics today have given up naturalistic theories.

st8.quote: I will use no data that are not strongly evidenced by many other pieces of data.

arguments.prior_art: Gary Habermas & Michael Licona, The Case for the Resurrection of Jesus, 2004

or1.quote: In our book, the resurre the case of the resurrection of Jesus, Mike Lacona and I do some wild ones
or1.why: This is Habermas's own signature minimal-facts argument, so it is a variant/continuation of his prior work rather than a new argument.

or2.quote: Most critics today have given up naturalistic theories.
or2.why: Adds the sociological claim that critics have abandoned naturalistic theories, and cites Crossley's concession.

or3.why: No cross-domain connection is made; the argument stays within historical apologetics.

or4.why: No formalization, equation or model is offered.

arguments.weakest_link: P2 (most critics have given up naturalistic theories) is a sociological generalization supported only by anecdote and named allies.
arguments.develop_next: Provide a systematic survey or citation count showing the proportion of critical scholars who affirm each minimal fact and reject naturalistic theories.

arguments.name: Christianity's early testimony is unique among world religions
arguments.conclusion: Christianity has earlier and better-attested historical sources than any other religion or ancient figure.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: The earliest sources for Alexander the Great are about 300 years after his death (S244).
P2: Buddhist sources are 600-800 years after Buddha (S256).
P3: Paul Barnett says nothing in ancient history, secular or religious, has anything like the early Christian testimony (S243).
P4: Even Bart Ehrman admits we have high Christology texts from 2-3 years after the cross (S266).

st1.quote: How early? early enough that no other religion in the world has anything like this.

st2.quote: Earliest date for Alexander that we have one of Alexander's writings about him just short of 300 years after he died.

st3.quote: Paul Barnett, an Australian historian, says he's taught world religions. He's taught ancient history. He says nothing in ancient history, secular or religious, has anything like this.

st4.quote: Bartman says, "We have several of these high christologology texts from two to three years after the cross."

st8.quote: Earliest date for Alexander that we have one of Alexander's writings about him just short of 300 years after he died.

arguments.prior_art: Paul Barnett, Is the New Testament Reliable?, 1986/2003

or1.quote: Paul Barnett, an Australian historian, says he's taught world religions.
or1.why: It largely restates Barnett's comparison of Christian and other ancient sources, adding a few named comparanda.

or2.quote: When you open up page one, here's what the book says to my Christian readers. We don't have what you have.
or2.why: Adds the Buddhist-scriptures quotation and Ehrman's 2-3 year high-Christology admission as data.

or3.why: No cross-domain connection beyond the historical comparison itself.

arguments.weakest_link: The comparison conflates 'earliest source date' with 'quality of attestation' and relies on a single authority (Barnett) for the sweeping uniqueness claim.
arguments.develop_next: Give a source-by-source table of composition-to-event gaps for the key figures/religions compared, with standard critical dating.
